en.title: Final Execution Counts of Referenced Commands
en.description:
Each entry is one of cmd1, cmd2, cmd3, or !j, which means executing the command represented by the j-th entry. Count how many times each of the three commands is ultimately executed over all entries. Valid input on this site guarantees that every reference chain eventually reaches an actual command; forward and backward references are allowed, but there are no reference cycles.

This site's standard input/output is stated explicitly; ranges not given by the source are all marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n command tokens, 1≤n≤100000 (this site's range); the j in !j is 1..n.
en.output: Output the execution counts of cmd1, cmd2, and cmd3, separated by spaces.
en.explanation: Example 1: cmd1, cmd2, and cmd3 are executed 3, 2, and 2 times respectively. Example 2: the first two entries both eventually reference the third entry, cmd2, so the output is 0 3 0. Example 3: there is only one cmd3, so the output is 0 0 1.
hints: Follow the reference chain until you reach an already resolved result, then mark every position on the path with that result. Finally, tally the command type of each position.
